summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) building high-performance C++ software for real-time, latency-sensitive systems. Experience with CUDA C++ kernel optimization, MPI distributed computing on SLURM-managed clusters, and Linux service deployment across networked, multi-device pipelines. Comfortable moving fast in small, focused engineering teams on high-visibility technical problems.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a distributed real-time pipeline across three layers — mobile client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and embedded controller — linked over a unified WebSocket fabric on the network.

Deployed the edge-side service as a systemd service (Type=simple, auto-restart with backoff, non-root user/group isolation, environment-file-based config) with static IP networking for reliable multi-device registration.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript conv layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights/biases, and preallocated global buffers to eliminate per-layer allocation overhead.
Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms vs 73.3ms (uncoalesced) and 77.5ms (CPU baseline) — ~35% speedup over naive GPU implementation with identical output accuracy.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Implemented and benchmarked four parallel work-distribution strategies in C++ (static strip/block/cyclic, dynamic task queue) using MPI for large-scale scene rendering.
Achieved up to 30× speedup with static strip partitioning (55 processes); showed dynamic task queueing outperformed all static strategies under unpredictable workloads.

projects.name: MPI Hodgkin-Huxley Neuron Simulation
bullets: Implemented distributed compute in C++ across MPI worker processes with synchronous state updates on a SLURM-managed cluster.
Achieved up to 10.49× speedup with 12 slave processes; characterized scaling behavior and identified load-imbalance effects causing up to 65% performance degradation under uneven work distribution.
